name: checkout-bad-deploy
input:
Customers reported that checkout was failing for a while this afternoon. Investigate the logs and write answer.json with exactly these fields:

{
  "endpoint": "METHOD /path of the failing endpoint, for example GET /api/v1/cart",
  "incident_start": "time of the first 5xx response on that endpoint, ISO 8601 UTC",
  "incident_end": "time of the last 5xx response on that endpoint, ISO 8601 UTC",
  "status_codes": [list of the distinct 5xx status codes it returned, as integers],
  "failed_requests": number of 5xx responses on that endpoint in the access log (integer),
  "bad_version": "the checkout-api version that caused it",
  "rollback_version": "the version that fixed it",
  "exception": "the exception class raised in the application"
}
checker:
cd /workspace 2>/dev/null || true
python3 - <<'FORGE_PY'
import json, os, re, sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

def fail(msg):
    print("FAIL: " + msg)
    sys.exit(1)

def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond:
        fail(msg)

def load_json(path):
    check(os.path.isfile(path), f"{path} was not written")
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except ValueError as exc:
        fail(f"{path} is not valid JSON: {exc}")

def field(obj, key, kind=None):
    check(isinstance(obj, dict), f"expected a JSON object, got {type(obj).__name__}")
    check(key in obj, f"missing field {key!r} (have {sorted(obj)})")
    value = obj[key]
    if kind is not None:
        ok = isinstance(value, kind) and not (kind in (int, float, (int, float)) and isinstance(value, bool))
        check(ok, f"field {key!r} has the wrong type: {value!r}")
    return value

def parse_time(value, what):
    check(isinstance(value, str), f"{what} should be an ISO 8601 string, got {value!r}")
    text = value.strip().replace(" ", "T")
    if text.endswith("Z"):
        text = text[:-1] + "+00:00"
    try:
        t = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
    except ValueError:
        fail(f"{what} is not ISO 8601: {value!r}")
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return t

def near_time(value, expected, tolerance_s, what):
    got = parse_time(value, what)
    want = parse_time(expected, what)
    delta = abs((got - want).total_seconds())
    check(delta <= tolerance_s, f"{what} is {value}, expected about {expected} (within {tolerance_s}s)")

def near(value, expected, tolerance, what):
    check(isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool), f"{what} should be a number: {value!r}")
    check(abs(value - expected) <= tolerance, f"{what} is {value}, expected {expected} (within {tolerance})")

def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(s)).strip().lower()
TRUTH = json.loads("{\"bad_version\": \"2.14.0\", \"endpoint\": \"POST /api/v1/checkout\", \"exception\": \"KeyError\", \"failed_requests\": 91, \"incident_end\": \"2026-09-14T14:38:22Z\", \"incident_start\": \"2026-09-14T14:03:23Z\", \"rollback_finished\": \"2026-09-14T14:39:32Z\", \"rollback_version\": \"2.13.4\", \"status_codes\": [500]}")
a = load_json("answer.json")
t = TRUTH
check(norm(field(a, "endpoint", str)) == norm(t["endpoint"]), f"endpoint is {a['endpoint']!r}, expected {t['endpoint']!r}")
near_time(field(a, "incident_start"), t["incident_start"], 120, "incident_start")
near_time(field(a, "incident_end"), t["incident_end"], 120, "incident_end")
codes = field(a, "status_codes", list)
check(sorted(set(codes)) == t["status_codes"], f"status_codes is {codes}, expected {t['status_codes']}")
check(field(a, "failed_requests", int) == t["failed_requests"], f"failed_requests is {a['failed_requests']}, expected {t['failed_requests']}")
check(str(field(a, "bad_version")).lstrip("v") == t["bad_version"], f"bad_version is {a['bad_version']!r}")
check(str(field(a, "rollback_version")).lstrip("v") == t["rollback_version"], f"rollback_version is {a['rollback_version']!r}")
check(str(field(a, "exception")).strip().split(":")[0].split(".")[-1] == t["exception"], f"exception is {a['exception']!r}")
print("PASS")
FORGE_PY

name: orders-slow-queries
input:
The orders page was very slow for some customers in the early morning. Find out why using the database log and write answer.json with exactly these fields:

{
  "spike_start": "time of the first statement slower than 1000 ms, ISO 8601 UTC",
  "spike_end": "time of the last statement slower than 1000 ms, ISO 8601 UTC",
  "application_name": "the Postgres application_name that caused the slowdown",
  "table": "the table its statements were scanning",
  "slow_statements": number of statements of any application slower than 1000 ms (integer),
  "max_duration_ms": the longest statement duration in milliseconds (number)
}

name: expiring-certificates
catalog-scraper
input:
Catalog latency complaints came in around the early evening, and we suspect a single client was hammering us. Find it and write answer.json with exactly these fields:

{
  "ip": "client IP address",
  "user_agent": "its full User-Agent string",
  "total_requests": number of requests from that IP in the access log (integer),
  "rate_limited": how many of them got HTTP 429 (integer),
  "first_seen": "time of its first request, ISO 8601 UTC",
  "last_seen": "time of its last request, ISO 8601 UTC"
}
